Overview

A 36-hour Generative AI Media Hackathon Hackathon in Bengaluru.

Zero to One is India's first Generative Media Hackathon, bringing together students, developers, AI engineers, designers, founders, and creators to build the next generation of AI-powered storytelling, audio, and visual experiences.

Presented by Pocket FM, in partnership with OpenAI, Lightspeed, Databricks and powered by Buildora, this 36-hour offline hackathon is where ambitious builders transform bold ideas into working products.

From keynote sessions and live demos to networking, Zero to One is designed to help participants go from an idea to a real prototype.

THE EXPERIENCE

  • Build alongside 300+ shortlisted builders during an intensive 36-hour hackathon.
  • Solve real-world challenges at the intersection of AI, storytelling, audio, and media.
  • Learn directly from founders, AI leaders, and industry experts.
  • Attend keynote sessions and an exclusive OpenAI session.
  • Present your solution before an expert jury during the final demo showcase.
  • Win exciting prizes and exclusive rewards.
  • Connect with fellow builders, founders, investors, and the AI community.

KEY SPEAKERS

Learn from the people building the future of AI and media.

  • Rohan Nayak — Co-Founder, Pocket FM
  • Prateek Dixit — Co-Founder, Pocket FM
  • Harsha Kumar — Partner, Lightspeed
  • Vasu Sharma — Head of AI, Pocket FM
  • Debasis Bhattacharya — Director of Field Engineering, Databricks

More speakers will be announced soon. Stay tuned!

ABOUT POCKET FM

Pocket FM is the world's leading entertainment series platform, pioneering serialized audio entertainment across languages and genres for millions of listeners every day. With AI at the heart of its content engine, Pocket FM is building the future of storytelling, and now, it's inviting you to build it too.

From storytelling to voice, creators to copilots, this is where the next generation of AI-powered media products goes from Zero to One.

  • Founders
  • Builders

  • Teams must consist of 3 to 4 members.
  • Solo participation is not permitted.

Rules

Please read the following rules carefully before participating in Zero to One.

1. Team Composition

  • Participation is team-based.
  • Each team must consist of 3 to 4 members.
  • Cross-college and cross-company teams are welcome.
  • Solo participation is not permitted.

2. Eligibility

Zero to One is open to students, AI engineers, software developers, designers, founders, and builders who are passionate about creating innovative AI-powered media experiences.

3. Registration & Shortlisting

  • Participation is free of charge.
  • All registrations must be completed before the registration deadline.
  • Applications will be screened by the organizing team.
  • Only shortlisted teams will be invited to participate in the offline finale.

4. Build During the Hackathon

Projects submitted for evaluation must be developed during the 36-hour hackathon. Participants may use open-source libraries, public APIs, and pretrained models, but the core solution should be built during the event.

5. Use of AI

Participants are encouraged to use AI models, tools, and assistants while building their solutions. Teams must clearly disclose the AI technologies, models, and services used during submission and project demonstrations.

6. Offline Participation

Shortlisted teams must attend the complete offline finale on 25–26 July 2026. Participants must carry a valid government-issued or college ID for verification during check-in.

7. Project Demonstration

Every team must present a working prototype during the final demo session. Projects will be evaluated based on innovation, technical execution, effective use of AI, real-world impact, and the quality of the demonstration.

8. Fair Play

Plagiarism, misrepresentation of work, or any form of unfair conduct will result in immediate disqualification. All participants are expected to maintain a respectful and collaborative environment throughout the hackathon.

9. Judging

The decisions of the judges and organizers are final and binding.

10. Organizer's Rights

The organizers reserve the right to modify the event schedule, rules, or guidelines if necessary. Any updates will be communicated through the official event page or via email to shortlisted participants.
